In the figure above, $∠BOA$ is a straight angle,  and $\overset{\to }{OC}$ is the bisector of $∠BOD.$ If $m∠DOA={58}^{∘},$ find $m∠COA.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237394/assets/9d7c5789c579b9292beb17ad03ae6239083ffa70fe5ec581da33cd488e365344.png)

Since the angles $∠BOD$ and $∠DOA$ are supplementary, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOD & ={180}^{∘}-m∠DOA \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{58}^{∘} \\  & ={122}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COD & =\frac{m∠BOD}{2} \\  & =\frac{{122}^{∘}}{2} \\  & ={61}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COA & =m∠COD+m∠DOA \\  & ={61}^{∘}+{58}^{∘} \\  & ={119}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
